sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Tryamour is an Arthurian heroine in the poetry of Marie de France. She is a fairy lover who gives wealth to the knight Launfal in return for his love. She made one demand of him. He must never boast of her. Launfal could not hold to that promise. Tryamour still was more kind than other fairies. She let him join her in the Otherworld.
